added_lemmas.statement: For a linear recursive structural equation model whose directed support is a rooted spanning tree and whose bidirected support is arbitrary (bows included), the randomized polynomial-time procedure of Gupta and Bl\"aser decides, for every queried directed coefficient, whether its generic single-coordinate degree is \(1\), \(2\), or infinite.  In each finite case it returns the corresponding one or two \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions for the queried coefficient.

added_lemmas.justification: This published result is the complete algorithmic substrate for the exact zero-excess class transfer.
added_lemmas.gap: It applies to rooted tree-shaped directed support, not to positive excess-parent budget.
added_lemmas.consumer: The zero-excess branch of the symbolic dispatcher uses its exact classification and finite expressions.

added_lemmas.statement: For every \(n\geq2\), the class \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) is exactly the rooted tree-shaped mixed-graph class, with arbitrary bidirected support, treated by the complete tree algorithm, up to the source paper's vertex-count indexing convention.  Consequently, on every input \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,0}\), that algorithm returns the exact value \(d_e(G)\in\{1,2,\infty\}\) and, when \(d_e(G)<\infty\), all one or two \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions for \(\lambda_e\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,0}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\), one has \(T\subseteq D\) and
\[
 |D\setminus T|\leq0.
\]
Cardinality is nonnegative, so \(D\setminus T=\varnothing\), whence \(D=T\).  The same definition, through \(\mathrm{ass:arborescence}\), says that \(T\) is a rooted spanning arborescence.  Thus the entire directed support \(D\) is a rooted spanning tree.  The definition of \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) imposes no restriction on \(B\), so its bidirected support is arbitrary and may contain a bow with an edge of \(D\).

Conversely, given any rooted tree-shaped mixed graph on \(n\) vertices and any queried directed edge \(e\), put \(T=D\).  Then \(T\) is a rooted spanning arborescence and \(|D\setminus T|=0\), so \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,0}\).  These two inclusions prove equality of the graph-query classes; changing whether the source counts the root separately is only an indexing relabeling and changes no graph.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:gupta\mbox{-}blaser\mbox{-}tree\mbox{-}classification}\) to this common class.  It returns the exact trichotomy \(d_e(G)=1\), \(d_e(G)=2\), or \(d_e(G)=\infty\), and in the first two cases it returns respectively one or two \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions.  This is a class transfer, not an extension of the tree theorem to any graph with \(|D\setminus T|>0\).
added_lemmas.justification: The dispatcher may invoke the published complete procedure only after equality of its graph class with the zero-excess class is proved.
added_lemmas.gap: The transfer is exact at zero excess and deliberately makes no positive-excess claim.
added_lemmas.consumer: The zero-excess branch of the fixed-parameter dispatcher returns the exact degree and finite expressions.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the multihomogeneous system used by \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), the query component has at most \(n-1\) nonempty child blocks and its binary-factor graph is simple.  For a simple graph on at most two blocks every prescribed-indegree coefficient is at most \(1\); on at most three blocks it is at most \(2\); and on at most four blocks it is at most \(4\), with
\[
 [X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq4}(X_i+X_j)=4.
\]
If \(n=5\) and \(|D\setminus T|\leq1\), the coefficient is at most \(3\).  Hence every finite queried-coordinate degree satisfies
\[
 d_e(G)\leq1\quad(n=3),\qquad
 d_e(G)\leq2\quad(n=4),\qquad
 d_e(G)\leq3\quad(n=5,\ |D\setminus T|\leq1),
\]
and \(d_e(G)\leq4\) when \(n=5\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For a finite simple graph \(H=(W,E_H)\) and a vector \(r=(r_v:v\in W)\) of nonnegative integers, define
\[
 c_H(r)=\left[\prod_{v\in W}X_v^{r_v}\right]
          \prod_{\{u,v\}\in E_H}(X_u+X_v).
\]
Choosing \(X_v\) from the factor indexed by \(\{u,v\}\) is the same as orienting that edge toward \(v\).  Therefore \(c_H(r)\) is exactly the number of orientations of \(H\) having indegree vector \(r\).  In particular it is zero unless
\[
 sum_{v\in W}r_v=|E_H|,
 qquad 0\leq r_v\leq\deg_H(v).
 \tag{1}
\]

If \(|W|\leq2\), simplicity gives at most one edge, and its orientation is fixed by its indegree vector.  Thus \(c_H(r)\leq1\).  If \(|W|\leq3\) and \(H\) is a forest, two distinct orientations with the same indegrees would have a nonempty balanced symmetric difference; following an edge in that difference would produce a cycle, contrary to acyclicity.  Hence the count is at most one.  The only remaining graph is the triangle.  Its two cyclic orientations both have indegree vector \((1,1,1)\), while every transitive orientation has a distinct labeled permutation of \((0,1,2)\).  Hence the maximum on three blocks is two.

Now suppose \(|W|\leq4\).  If \(|E_H|\leq4\), the graph has at most one independent cycle: a graph with two edge-disjoint cycle contributions on four vertices would have cyclomatic number at least two and hence at least five edges.  After the orientations of the attached forest edges are fixed by the prescribed indegrees from the leaves inward, the sole cycle, if present, has at most its two cyclic orientations.  Thus the argument componentwise gives
\[
 c_H(r)\leq2qquad (|E_H|\leq4).
 \tag{2}
\]
For five edges, \(H=K_4\setminus\{1,2\}\).  Directly expanding
\[
 (X_1+X_3)(X_1+X_4)(X_2+X_3)(X_2+X_4)(X_3+X_4)
\]
and first fixing the exponents \((r_1,r_2)=(a,b)\in\{0,1,2\}^2\) gives the following maxima over the remaining two exponents:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
  &b=0&b=1&b=2\\ \hline
 a=0&1&2&1\\
 a=1&2&3&2\\
 a=2&1&2&1
 \end{array}.
 \tag{3}
\]
For completeness, each entry in (3) follows by choosing the \(a\) factors among \(X_1+X_3,X_1+X_4\) that contribute \(X_1\), choosing the \(b\) factors among \(X_2+X_3,X_2+X_4\) that contribute \(X_2\), and then making the two possible choices in \(X_3+X_4\); collecting equal exponent pairs gives the displayed table.  Thus every five-edge coefficient is at most three.  In the positive-capacity case relevant below, (1) forces a permutation of \((2,1,1,1)\), and equality three occurs precisely when the exponent two is on vertex \(3\) or \(4\), a vertex not incident to the missing edge.

For six edges, \(H=K_4\).  The possible sorted exponent patterns satisfying (1) are
\[
 (0,0,3,3),\quad(0,1,2,3),\quad(0,2,2,2),
 \quad(1,1,1,3),\quad(1,1,2,2).
\]
The first has coefficient zero because the edge joining the two zero-exponent vertices has nowhere to point.  A labeled vector of type \((0,1,2,3)\) has one transitive orientation.  In types \((0,2,2,2)\) and \((1,1,1,3)\), the edges incident to the extreme vertex are forced and the remaining triangle has its two cyclic orientations.  Finally, for \(r=(1,1,2,2)\), conditioning on the factor \(X_1+X_2\) gives
\[
 [X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{i<j}(X_i+X_j)=2+2=4:
\]
if that factor contributes \(X_1\), the factors on edges \(13,14\) must contribute \(X_3X_4\), after which the triangle on \(2,3,4\) has two cyclic choices; the case in which it contributes \(X_2\) is symmetric.  This proves the four-block maximum four and its attainment.

It remains to connect these counts to the SEM bound.  In the square subsystem selected in the proof of \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), variables are blocked by their child vertex.  A rooted arborescence has one root, so there are at most \(n-1\) nonempty child blocks.  A residual \(F_{ij}\) has degree at most one in either child block, and an unordered pair of blocks supplies at most one selected binary residual; hence the binary-factor graph is simple.  The multihomogeneous B\'ezout lemma identifies its coefficient with the orientation count just bounded.

For \(n=5\) and \(|D\setminus T|\leq1\), one has \(|D|\leq5\).  The square subsystem therefore has at most five factors after the unary factors are removed.  With at most four binary factors, (2) gives the stronger bound two.  With five binary factors there can be no unary factor, all four blocks must occur, their positive block capacities sum to five, and hence the only capacity pattern is a permutation of \((2,1,1,1)\); (3) bounds its coefficient by three.  Combining this with the two-, three-, and four-block bounds gives all displayed consequences for \(d_e(G)\).
added_lemmas.justification: These exact orientation coefficients sharpen the general power-of-two ceiling at three, four, and five vertices.
added_lemmas.gap: The calculation bounds the existing multihomogeneous system; it does not assert that every orientation maximum is realizable by an SEM.
added_lemmas.consumer: The exact small-size frontier uses these bounds to match the tree, cubic, and quartic witnesses.

added_lemmas.statement: Example 8 and Figure 5(b) of Foygel, Draisma, and Drton exhibit an acyclic five-vertex linear structural equation model whose directed support consists of five arrows and contains a rooted spanning arborescence, and whose generic covariance parametrization has degree three.  Equivalently, its source function field is a degree-three extension of its covariance function field.

added_lemmas.justification: The published degree-three example supplies the five-vertex, one-excess lower-bound substrate.
added_lemmas.gap: The source states whole-fiber degree; the coordinate-degree consequence requires the separate transfer lemma.
added_lemmas.consumer: The coordinate transfer and exact five-vertex frontier use this published base case.

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a graph-query \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,1}\) for which \(d_e(G)=3\).  In particular,
\[
 D_1(5)\geq3,
\]
and one original directed coefficient separates the three characteristic-zero conjugate branches.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(\widetilde G\) be the graph in \(\mathrm{lem:foygel\mbox{-}five\mbox{-}node\mbox{-}degree\mbox{-}three}\).  Its directed support has five arrows and contains a rooted spanning arborescence \(T\), which has four arrows on five vertices.  Hence
\[
 |D\setminus T|=5-4=1,
\]
and \((\widetilde G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,1}\) for every directed edge query \(e\) of \(\widetilde G\).

Write \(K_{\widetilde G}\subset L_{\widetilde G}\) for the covariance and source function fields.  The cited degree statement gives
\[
 [L_{\widetilde G}:K_{\widetilde G}]=3.
 \tag{4}
\]
For fixed \(\Sigma\) and \(\Lambda\), the noise matrix is not an additional fiber choice, because the covariance equation rearranges to
\[
 \Omega=(I_5-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_5-\Lambda).
 \tag{5}
\]
If every directed coordinate \(\lambda_f\) belonged to \(K_{\widetilde G}\), then (5) would put every allowed noise coordinate in \(K_{\widetilde G}\) as well.  Since the source field is generated by the directed and allowed noise coordinates, this would give \(L_{\widetilde G}=K_{\widetilde G}\), contradicting (4).  Thus some original directed edge \(e\) satisfies \(\lambda_e\notin K_{\widetilde G}\).

The tower law and (4) give
\[
 [K_{\widetilde G}(\lambda_e):K_{\widetilde G}]
 \mid [L_{\widetilde G}:K_{\widetilde G}]=3.
\]
The left side is greater than one, so primality of three forces it to equal three.  Therefore \(d_e(\widetilde G)=3\), proving the lower bound.  The ground field has characteristic zero, so the degree-three minimal polynomial is separable; its three roots are the images of \(\lambda_e\) under the three covariance-field embeddings and are distinct.  Thus this original edge coordinate separates all three conjugate branches.
added_lemmas.justification: Prime whole-fiber degree three forces any varying original coordinate to have degree three.
added_lemmas.gap: This is a transfer of a published example and is not claimed as a new graph construction.
added_lemmas.consumer: It attains the upper bound for \(D_1(5)\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(G^{(4)}\) have vertices \(0,1,2,3,4\),
\[
 D=\{0\to1,0\to2,1\to3,2\to3,1\to4,2\to4\},
 \qquad
 B=\{0\leftrightarrow i:1\leq i\leq4\},
\]
and let
\[
 T=\{0\to1,0\to2,1\to3,1\to4\},
 \qquad e=2\to4.
\]
Then \((G^{(4)},T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,2}\) and \(d_e(G^{(4)})=4\).  The four conjugates are simple and have distinct queried coordinates.  Appending any number of fully bidirected children of \(0\), placing their arrows in \(T\), preserves this coordinate degree.  Consequently \(D_k(5)\geq4\) for every admissible \(k\geq2\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The set \(T\) has four edges, gives every nonroot vertex exactly one parent, and has directed paths from \(0\) to all vertices.  Thus it is a rooted spanning arborescence.  The two edges \(2\to3\) and \(2\to4\) are exactly \(D\setminus T\), the directed graph is acyclic in the displayed vertex order, and \(e\in D\).  Hence \((G^{(4)},T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,2}\).

Write
\[
 (a,b,c,d,u,f)
 =\bigl(\lambda_{01},\lambda_{02},\lambda_{13},
         \lambda_{23},\lambda_{14},\lambda_{24}\bigr).
\]
At the rational source point
\[
 (a,b,c,d,u,f)=(2,3,4,5,6,7),
\]
take disturbance diagonal \((30,31,32,33,34)\), take \(\omega_{0i}=i\) for \(1\leq i\leq4\), and set every other off-diagonal disturbance entry to zero.  For every real vector \(x\), the inequality \(2|x_ix_j|\leq x_i^2+x_j^2\) gives
\[
 x^{\mathsf T}\Omega x
 \geq \sum_{i=0}^4
 \left(\omega_{ii}-\sum_{j\ne i}|\omega_{ij}|\right)x_i^2>0,
\]
because the five diagonal margins are respectively \(20,30,30,30,30\).  Thus \(\Omega\) is positive definite.  Direct multiplication in the defining covariance formula gives
\[
 \Sigma_0=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 30&61&92&707&1014\\
 61&155&187&1561&2247\\
 92&187&314&2327&3332\\
 707&1561&2327&17981&25747\\
 1014&2247&3332&25747&36972
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{6}
\]

The missing bidirected pairs are precisely the six pairs among \(1,2,3,4\).  Substitution of (6) into their residuals gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 F_{12}&=30ab-92a-61b+187,\\
 F_{13}&=61ac+92ad-707a-155c-187d+1561,\\
 F_{14}&=61au+92af-1014a-155u-187f+2247,\\
 F_{23}&=61bc+92bd-707b-187c-314d+2327,\\
 F_{24}&=61bu+92bf-1014b-187u-314f+3332,\\
 F_{34}&=155cu+187cf-2247c+187du+314df-3332d
          -1561u-2327f+25747.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
Exact rational Buchberger reduction of (7), in lexicographic order eliminating \(a,b,c,d,u\) before \(f\), gives the following five linear relations:
\[
\begin{aligned}
0={}&384915840a+425450175590061f^3-8965411803407607f^2\\
&+62974399432228195f-147445028655847225,\\
0={}&741827520b-593375419233f^3+12321625507347f^2\\
&-85271405126447f+196665729339485,\\
0={}&615040c+25798931271f^3-543666188277f^2\\
&+3818873142057f-8941504654939,\\
0={}&4d-3f+1,\\
0={}&153760u+8599643757f^3-181222062759f^2\\
&+1272957714019f-2980501654153,
\end{aligned}
 \tag{8}
\]
together with
\[
 q(f)=(f-7)\bigl(8599643757f^3-181150021425f^2
             +1271943861499f-2976933819575\bigr).
 \tag{9}
\]
This calculation is an exact ideal certificate: reducing each polynomial in (7) by (8)--(9) gives zero, and the Buchberger \(S\)-polynomial reductions of (8)--(9) are zero, so (8)--(9) generate the specialized residual ideal.  The Euclidean algorithm in \(\mathbb Q[f]\) gives
\[
 \gcd(q,q')=1.
 \tag{10}
\]
Equations (8) have nonzero constant leading coefficients and recover exactly one value of \(a,b,c,d,u\) from each root of \(q\).  Equations (9)--(10) therefore identify the specialized quotient with the product of four reduced residue fields over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\); in particular there are four simple points with four distinct \(f\)-coordinates.  The original source point is the point with \(f=7\), so the specialized incidence fiber is nonempty.

At each of these reduced zero-dimensional points, the differentials of the six generators (7) span the six-dimensional cotangent space.  Equivalently, the residual Jacobian with respect to \((a,b,c,d,u,f)\) has rank six.  A nonzero Jacobian minor remains nonzero on a Zariski neighborhood, so these four distinct coordinate branches persist over a common nonempty covariance open set.  It follows that the generic queried-coordinate extension is algebraic and has degree at least four.  On the other hand, \(\mathrm{lem:small\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}maxima}\) gives degree at most four for every finite query on five vertices.  Consequently
\[
 d_{\,2\to4}(G^{(4)})=4.
 \tag{11}
\]
The incidence-localization theorem ensures that this conclusion concerns the source-prime generic fiber and that no directed-coordinate value has been discarded by a source-coordinate saturation.  The squarefreeness in (10) proves simplicity and distinctness of the four conjugates.

Finally append a new vertex \(w\) with the sole directed edge \(0\to w\), place that edge in \(T\), and allow \(w\) to be bidirected with every old vertex.  There is then no new missing-bidirected residual involving \(w\), so all old residuals (7) are unchanged.  More explicitly, the new covariance coordinates \(\sigma_{iw}\) and \(\sigma_{ww}\) can replace the freely allowed new noise coordinates by a triangular rational change of variables, while \(\lambda_{0w}\) remains free.  Hence the enlarged covariance field is a purely transcendental extension of the old covariance field independent of \(f\).  Minimal-polynomial degree is unchanged under such a regular purely transcendental base extension, so (11) remains degree four.  Iteration proves the appending claim.  At \(n=5\), class inclusion \(\mathcal G_{5,2}\subseteq\mathcal G_{5,k}\) for \(k\geq2\) gives \(D_k(5)\geq4\).
added_lemmas.justification: The exact rational calculation supplies the sharp two-excess lower bound and a reusable characteristic-zero regression witness.
added_lemmas.gap: It establishes one attaining orbit, not an exhaustive census of all five-vertex rooted graph-query orbits.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every admissible pair with \(2\leq n\leq5\), the exact sharp coordinate-degree frontier is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 n & D_k(n)\\ \hline
 2 & D_0(2)=1,\\
 3 & D_k(3)=1\quad(0\leq k\leq1),\\
 4 & D_k(4)=2\quad(0\leq k\leq3),\\
 5 & D_0(5)=2,\quad D_1(5)=3,\quad D_k(5)=4\quad(2\leq k\leq6).
\end{array}
\]
In each nontrivial lower-bound construction an original directed coefficient separates all generic conjugate branches.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The admissible range is \(0\leq k\leq(n-1)(n-2)/2\).  For \(n=2\), this forces \(k=0\), and \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\) gives \(D_0(2)=1\).

For \(n=3\), \(k\in\{0,1\}\).  The two-block conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:small\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}maxima}\) gives \(d_e(G)\leq1\) for every finite query in either class.  The inclusion \(\mathcal G_{3,0}\subseteq\mathcal G_{3,k}\), together with the tree witness \(D_0(3)=1\) from \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\), gives the reverse inequality.  Hence \(D_k(3)=1\).

For \(n=4\), the three-block bound gives \(d_e(G)\leq2\) for every finite query and every admissible \(k\).  The same class inclusion and the separating degree-two tree witness in \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\) give \(D_k(4)\geq2\).  Thus \(D_k(4)=2\) for \(0\leq k\leq3\).

For \(n=5,k=0\), the tree result gives \(D_0(5)=2\).  For \(k=1\), the special five-edge bound in \(\mathrm{lem:small\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}maxima}\) gives \(D_1(5)\leq3\), while \(\mathrm{lem:five\mbox{-}node\mbox{-}cubic\mbox{-}coordinate\mbox{-}transfer}\) supplies a graph and an original edge of degree three.  Hence \(D_1(5)=3\).  Finally, for every admissible \(k\geq2\), the general four-block bound gives \(D_k(5)\leq4\), and \(\mathrm{lem:five\mbox{-}node\mbox{-}quartic\mbox{-}witness}\), together with \(\mathcal G_{5,2}\subseteq\mathcal G_{5,k}\), gives \(D_k(5)\geq4\).  Thus \(D_k(5)=4\).  The cited tree witnesses, the cubic transfer, and the quartic witness each identify the separating original coefficient asserted in the theorem.
added_lemmas.justification: The exact table removes every vertex size through five from the unresolved frontier.
added_lemmas.gap: The remaining orientation-realization issue begins at six vertices with positive excess budget in the small-size strip.
added_lemmas.consumer: The frontier open question and the software ambiguity budget use these exact base cases.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every admissible \(k\) and every \(n\geq4\),
\[
 D_k(n)\geq
 2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}.
\]
The lower bound is attained within the one-sink family by one original directed coefficient.  At \(n=5\), the separate exact values are the sharper conclusions \(D_1(5)=3\) and \(D_k(5)=4\) for \(k\geq2\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 j=\min\{k,\lfloor(n-4)/2\rfloor\}.
\]
Then \(j\leq k\) and \(n\geq2j+4\).  Apply \(\mathrm{thm:large\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\) with excess budget \(j\).  The one-sink graph \(G^{\star}_{j,n}\) belongs to \(\mathcal G_{n,j}\), and its original edge \(e^{\star}\) satisfies
\[
 d_{e^{\star}}(G^{\star}_{j,n})=2^{j+1}.
\]
Because an input with at most \(j\) excess arrows also has at most \(k\) excess arrows,
\[
 \mathcal G_{n,j}\subseteq\mathcal G_{n,k},
\]
and therefore \(D_k(n)\geq2^{j+1}\).  For every integer \(n\geq4\),
\[
 \lfloor(n-4)/2\rfloor+1=\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor,
\]
so
\[
 j+1=\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}.
\]
Substitution proves the displayed envelope.  The final five-vertex values follow independently from \(\mathrm{thm:small\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\), and are stated separately because they exceed the one-sink envelope there.
added_lemmas.justification: Class monotonicity turns the large-size one-sink construction into a certified lower bound at every size.
added_lemmas.gap: The envelope need not be sharp in the remaining strip, as the sharper five-vertex cubic and quartic values demonstrate.
added_lemmas.consumer: Any eventual all-size recurrence must dominate this explicit lower envelope.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For the remaining unsettled regime \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\), use \(\mathsf{FrontierHandle}\) to determine an explicit formula or finite structural recurrence solely in \(n,k\) for \(D_k(n)\).  Prove a matching universal upper bound, construct for every remaining pair a graph-query family in \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) attaining it, and prove that one original directed coefficient separates the retained generic branches.  The recurrence must account for forced covariance relations, losses under exact \(S_G\)-localization and affine dehomogenization, and roots at projective infinity; it must dominate
\[
 2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}},
\]
agree with the exact table in \(\mathrm{thm:small\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\), and agree with \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) when \(n\geq2k+4\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original all-size question is obsolete on \(k=0\), on every \(n\leq5\), and on \(n\geq2k+4\), because those regimes are now proved.  The only honest unresolved scope is the positive-excess strip with \(n\geq6\) and \(n<2k+4\).

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), first compute \(r=|D\setminus T|\).  If \(r=0\), use the complete tree-class procedure transferred in \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}algorithm\mbox{-}transfer}\): return the exact tag \(d_e(G)\in\{1,2,\infty\}\), and, when \(d_e(G)<\infty\), return the corresponding one or two \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions for \(\lambda_e\).  If \(r>0\), construct the acyclic covariance parametrization in the source coordinates, form its Jacobian and the Jacobian augmented by the row of \(\lambda_e\), and compute their generic ranks by independently randomized exact source specializations.  On this positive-excess branch return \((\operatorname{algebraic},\mathcal J_{G,e},2^{|D|-n+2})\) when the ranks agree and return \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\) when the augmented rank is larger.  The transcript \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\) records the specialization, pivot minors, and source identity tests; \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) additionally records the augmented minor witnessing dominance.  The positive-excess algebraic branch does not compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The existing construction discards the complete published output on the exactly equal zero-excess tree class.  The corrected dispatcher restores that exact branch while leaving the positive-excess Jacobian tag unchanged.

prose_updates.tldr: Adding parents to a supplied rooted tree creates finite ambiguity measured here by the single-coordinate complex degree \(D_k(n)\), not by whole-fiber cardinality or real root count.  The paper proves the universal \(2^{k+1}\) ceiling, the equality \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) for \(n\geq2k+4\), the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact frontier for every \(n\leq5\). project_justification.fill: The paper proves the projection-aware degree upper bound, the large-size equality, the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact \(n\leq5\) coordinate-degree frontier. It isolates the remaining positive-\(k\), \(n\geq6\) small-size frontier in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\). It supplies an unconditional randomized Jacobian-rank tag, retains the complete published tree-case output at \(k=0\), and proves a conditional geometric-resolution theorem with explicit straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. Exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results hold only on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain.

prose_updates.related_work: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced TreeID for tree-shaped linear SEMs; Gupta and Bläser proved the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite-expression algorithm, and Briefs and Bläser accelerated the same tree-only predicate in fasttreeid.  That published tree class is exactly \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\), up to a harmless vertex-count indexing shift, and is not \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) for positive \(k\).  Foygel, Draisma, and Drton give the published five-node whole-fiber cubic used here as the \(D_1(5)\) base case; their cubic and other small higher-degree examples are not novelty claims.  Hollering, Misra, and Sturma optimize bounded-degree rational formulas, which is a different degree notion.  Giusti, Lecerf, and Salvy compute geometric resolutions for reduced regular sequences away from an inequation, and Lecerf treats arbitrary equations and inequations with complexity charged to intermediate geometric degree; neither selects the embedded source component or manufactures its source-nonzero chart.  The conditional real-set and inference rung is informed by identified-set and influence-function work but covers every retained branch without claiming discriminant-uniform inference or automatic branch selection.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact frontier is still unknown only for positive \(k\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\): the orientation coefficient may lose branches through forced covariance relations, exact localization, affine dehomogenization, or projective infinity.  The exhaustive five-node orbit census is now a secondary regression and coordinate-census question, not a kill test for the numerical frontier, because the cubic and quartic base cases and the entire \(n\leq5\) frontier are fixed.  Independently, the quadratic core does not construct a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\).  The exceptional-set theorem, real-root-lifting theorem, regular-cell lemma, derived root-separation lemma, regular finite-set inference theorem, and singleton inference proposition are proved conditional on a supplied valid chart and successful conditional output; none is claimed unconditionally.  Coordinate localization is never promoted to equality of full fibers, real roots are never equated with real supported lifts, and local rank is not used to assert real uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves the full frontier through five vertices, the all-size lower envelope, and the large-size equality, but not the remaining positive-excess small-size strip.  Unconditionally, the dispatcher returns the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions on \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\).  For \(|D\setminus T|>0\), it returns only a randomized algebraic-versus-transcendental tag, a rank or dominance certificate, and the degree ceiling; it does not return \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch.  Given valid source-prime charts and successful output, the conditional geometric-resolution theorem returns those exact finite objects with its stated straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence.  On precisely that same conditional domain, the six exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results are proved.  No discriminant-uniform inference, automatic branch selection, or all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed, and positive definiteness of recovered noise follows only after a complete real supported lift by congruence.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(G=(V,D,B)\) have \(V=\{0,1,2,3,4\}\),
\[
D=\{0\to1,0\to2,1\to3,2\to3,1\to4,2\to4\},
\qquad
B=\{0\leftrightarrow i:1\leq i\leq4\},
\]
let \(T=\{0\to1,0\to2,1\to3,1\to4\}\), and query \(e=2\to4\), with \(f=\lambda_e\).  Then \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,2}\) and \(d_e(G)=4\).  More precisely, at the displayed rational positive-definite specialization \(\Sigma^\star\) in the proof, the fiber obtained from \(A_K\) has four reduced points with distinct real \(f\)-coordinates, the roots of
\[
q(f)=(f-7)\bigl(8599643757f^3-181150021425f^2+1271943861499f-2976933819575\bigr).
\]
Every one of these four roots extends to real directed coefficients and a positive-definite disturbance matrix \(\Omega\) with support \(B\).  Moreover, for every integer \(N\geq5\), adjoining \(N-5\) new children of the root and making every pair incident with a new vertex bidirected produces a graph-query triple in \(\mathcal G_{N,2}\) whose queried degree is still four; consequently the same triple belongs to \(\mathcal G_{N,k}\) for every admissible \(k\geq2\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
(a,b,c,d,u,f)=(\lambda_{01},\lambda_{02},\lambda_{13},
\lambda_{23},\lambda_{14},\lambda_{24}).
\]
The order \(0<1<2<3<4\) is topological for \(D\), and \(T\) is a rooted spanning arborescence with root \(0\).  Since
\[
D\setminus T=\{2\to3,2\to4\},
\]
the definition of \(\mathcal G_{5,2}\) proves \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,2}\).

Consider the rational source point
\[
(a,b,c,d,u,f)=(2,3,4,5,6,7),
\qquad
\Omega^\star=
\begin{pmatrix}
30&1&2&3&4\\
1&31&0&0&0\\
2&0&32&0&0\\
3&0&0&33&0\\
4&0&0&0&34
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For every \(x\in\mathbb R^5\), the inequality \(2|x_i x_j|\leq x_i^2+x_j^2\) gives
\[
x^{\mathsf T}\Omega^\star x
\geq 20x_0^2+30x_1^2+30x_2^2+30x_3^2+30x_4^2.
\]
Thus \(\Omega^\star\) is positive definite.  Direct multiplication in the defining covariance parametrization gives
\[
\Sigma^\star=(I_5-\Lambda^\star)^{-\mathsf T}
\Omega^\star(I_5-\Lambda^\star)^{-1}
=\begin{pmatrix}
30&61&92&707&1014\\
61&155&187&1561&2247\\
92&187&314&2327&3332\\
707&1561&2327&17981&25747\\
1014&2247&3332&25747&36972
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The only missing bidirected pairs are the six pairs among \(\{1,2,3,4\}\).  Substitution of \(\Sigma^\star\) into their six residual polynomials \(F_{ij}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
r_{12}&=30ab-92a-61b+187,\\
r_{13}&=61ac+92ad-707a-155c-187d+1561,\\
r_{14}&=61au+92af-1014a-155u-187f+2247,\\
r_{23}&=61bc+92bd-707b-187c-314d+2327,\\
r_{24}&=61bu+92bf-1014b-187u-314f+3332,\\
r_{34}&=155cu+187cf-2247c+187du+314df-3332d\\
&\hspace{2.8em}{}-1561u-2327f+25747.
\end{aligned}
\]
Exact Buchberger reduction over \(\mathbb Q\), in lexicographic order \(a>b>c>d>u>f\), gives the following basis of the ideal \(J^\star=(r_{12},r_{13},r_{14},r_{23},r_{24},r_{34})\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_a={}&384915840a+425450175590061f^3-8965411803407607f^2\\
&{}+62974399432228195f-147445028655847225,\\
g_b={}&741827520b-593375419233f^3+12321625507347f^2\\
&{}-85271405126447f+196665729339485,\\
g_c={}&615040c+25798931271f^3-543666188277f^2\\
&{}+3818873142057f-8941504654939,\\
g_d={}&4d-3f+1,\\
g_u={}&153760u+8599643757f^3-181222062759f^2\\
&{}+1272957714019f-2980501654153,\\
g_f={}&8599643757f^4-241347527724f^3+2539994011474f^2\\
&{}-11880540850068f+20838536737025.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is an exact certificate: division of each \(r_{ij}\) by the displayed list has zero remainder, division in the reverse direction gives every \(g_\bullet\) as an element of \(J^\star\), and every pairwise \(S\)-polynomial reduces to zero.  In particular,
\[
g_f=q(f)
=(f-7)\bigl(8599643757f^3-181150021425f^2
+1271943861499f-2976933819575\bigr).
\]
If the cubic factor is denoted by \(c(f)\), exact integer arithmetic gives
\[
c(7)=-30256,
\qquad
\operatorname{disc}(c)
=1802165059445823134111101206528>0.
\]
Hence \(c\) has three distinct real roots and none is \(7\).  Thus \(q\) has four distinct real roots.  Since the leading coefficients of \(g_a,g_b,g_c,g_d,g_u\) in their respective non-\(f\) variables are nonzero rational integers, each root of \(q\) determines exactly one value of each of \(a,b,c,d,u\).  Consequently
\[
\mathbb C[a,b,c,d,u,f]/J^\star\cong\mathbb C[f]/(q)
\cong\mathbb C^4,
\]
so the specialized residual fiber consists of four reduced points with pairwise distinct \(f\)-coordinates.  Equivalently, at each point the cotangent space of the fiber is zero.  Because the six residuals generate \(J^\star\), their \(6\)-by-\(6\) Jacobian with respect to \((a,b,c,d,u,f)\) therefore has full rank at every one of the four points.

We next pass from this exact specialization to the generic coordinate degree.  Write the six variables in four blocks
\[
A=(a),\qquad B_0=(b),\qquad C=(c,d),\qquad U=(u,f),
\]
of respective sizes \((1,1,2,2)\).  Each residual indexed by a pair of distinct blocks has degree at most one in each of those two blocks and degree zero in the other two.  The multihomogeneous isolated-zero bound is therefore
\[
[X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq4}(X_i+X_j).
\]
In the edge order \((12,13,14,23,24,34)\), choosing an endpoint from each factor has exponent vector \((1,1,2,2)\) precisely for the following four endpoint lists:
\[
(1,3,4,2,4,3),\quad
(1,3,4,3,2,4),\quad
(2,1,4,3,4,3),\quad
(2,3,1,3,4,4).
\]
Thus
\[
[X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{i<j}(X_i+X_j)=4.
\]

For completeness, the lower-bound passage does not rely on an exceptional-fiber count.  Let \(s\) denote the fifteen symmetric covariance coordinates and let \(R(s,a,b,c,d,u,f)\) be the six-residual map.  At each of the four points over \(s=\Sigma^\star\), its coefficient Jacobian is invertible.  On writing \(s=\Sigma^\star+z\) and seeking a formal solution \(v=v_0+\sum_{r\geq1}v_r(z)\), homogeneous of degree \(r\) in \(z\), the degree-\(r\) equation is
\[
\left.\frac{\partial R}{\partial v}\right|_{(\Sigma^\star,v_0)}v_r
=-H_r(v_1,\ldots,v_{r-1};z),
\]
where the right-hand side is already determined by lower degrees.  Invertibility gives a unique \(v_r\) recursively.  Hence the four reduced points produce four formal branches over \(\mathbb C[[z]]\), and their \(f\)-series remain distinct because their constant terms are distinct.

The incidence space is irreducible: the change of coordinates
\[
\Omega=(I_5-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_5-\Lambda)
\]
is polynomial with polynomial inverse in the acyclic case, and imposing the six missing-noise entries sets six independent \(\Omega\)-coordinates equal to zero.  The four formal sections show that its covariance projection is dominant and generically zero-dimensional; in particular \(P_G=(0)\) here and \(K_G=\mathbb C(s)\).  The multihomogeneous calculation bounds the generic full fiber, counted with multiplicity, by four, whereas the four formal branches bound it below by four.  It therefore has degree four.  The four induced embeddings have distinct images of \(f\), so
\[
[K_G(f):K_G]\geq4.
\]
The coordinate degree cannot exceed the full-fiber degree, and hence \(d_e(G)=4\).

All four specialized coefficient vectors are real.  For any one of them let \(\widetilde\Lambda\) be the resulting acyclic coefficient matrix and set
\[
\widetilde\Omega=(I_5-\widetilde\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}
\Sigma^\star(I_5-\widetilde\Lambda).
\]
The residual equations give \(\widetilde\Omega_{ij}=0\) for every missing bidirected pair.  Also \(\Sigma^\star\) is positive definite, and \(I_5-\widetilde\Lambda\) is invertible because it is unit triangular in a topological order.  Congruence therefore makes \(\widetilde\Omega\) positive definite.  Thus all four real roots have real, support-valid, positive-definite extensions; no assertion of uniqueness follows from this fact.

Finally, adjoin a set \(W\) of \(N-5\) vertices, add \(0\to w\) to both \(D\) and \(T\) for every \(w\in W\), and put every bidirected pair having at least one endpoint in \(W\) into \(B\).  The enlarged directed graph is acyclic, the enlarged \(T\) is a rooted spanning arborescence, and the two old arrows \(2\to3\) and \(2\to4\) remain the only excess arrows.  Let \(Z\) be the new observed covariance coordinates and \(X=(\lambda_{0w}:w\in W)\).  Conditional on the old source field and on \(X\), the congruence formula above is a polynomially invertible change between the new unrestricted noise coordinates and \(Z\).  Therefore \(X\) and \(Z\) are algebraically independent over the old source field, and the enlarged observed field is the purely transcendental extension \(K_G(Z)\).  Irreducibility of the old minimal polynomial is preserved under a purely transcendental field extension by the coefficient-content argument.  Consequently
\[
[K_G(Z)(\lambda_e):K_G(Z)]=[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]=4.
\]
This proves the extension and, because the graph has two excess arrows, its membership in every admissible budget class with \(k\geq2\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
r=|D\setminus T|,
\qquad
u=(\lambda_D,\omega_B,\omega_{\mathrm{diag}}),
\qquad
N=|D|+|B|+n.
\]
The source coordinates are algebraically independent, so \(L=\mathbb C(u_1,\ldots,u_N)\). Acyclicity gives a topological ordering in which \(\Lambda\) is strictly triangular. Hence \(\Lambda^n=0\), and therefore
\[
(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}=I_n+\Lambda+\cdots+\Lambda^{n-1}.
\]
For \(i\leq j\), put
\[
s_{ij}(u)=\phi_G(\sigma_{ij})
=\left[(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}\right]_{ij}.
\]
Each entry of either inverse has directed-coordinate degree at most \(n-1\). Each summand of \(s_{ij}\) contains one disturbance coordinate and at most \(2n-2\) directed coordinates, so \(s_{ij}\) is a polynomial of total degree at most \(2n-1\). The nilpotent sum and the two matrix products give arithmetic circuits of size polynomial in \(n\).

Let \(s=(s_{ij}:i\leq j)\), let \(J_0=\partial s/\partial u\), and let \(J_1\) be obtained from \(J_0\) by adjoining the row \(\partial\lambda_e/\partial u\). Every entry of these matrices has total degree at most \(2n-2\). We now establish the rank criterion used by the dispatcher.

For arbitrary \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in L\), choose a maximal algebraically independent subfamily \(b_1,\ldots,b_q\) of the \(a_i\). Then every \(a_i\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb C(b_1,\ldots,b_q)\). Extend \(b_1,\ldots,b_q\) to a transcendence basis
\[
b_1,\ldots,b_q,c_1,\ldots,c_ell
\]
of \(L/\mathbb C\). Because the characteristic is zero, the algebraic extension of \(\mathbb C(b_1,ldots,b_q,c_1,ldots,c_ell)\) inside \(L\) is separable. For each \(j\), the derivation that differentiates with respect to \(b_j\) and fixes the other basis elements extends uniquely to \(L\): if \(v\) has minimal polynomial \(g(x)=\sum_h g_hx^h\), differentiating \(g(v)=0\) yields
\[
g'(v)\,dv=-\sum_h v^h\,d g_h,
\]
and separability gives \(g'(v)\ne0\). Applying these extended derivations to an \(L\)-linear relation among \(db_1,\ldots,db_q\) shows that every coefficient is zero. Thus these differentials are linearly independent. Conversely, differentiating the separable minimal polynomial of each \(a_i\) over \(\mathbb C(b_1,ldots,b_q)\) expresses \(da_i\) in their \(L\)-span. It follows that
\[
\dim_L\operatorname{span}_L\{da_1,\ldots,da_m\}
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(a_1,ldots,a_m).
\]

The rows of \(J_0\) and \(J_1\) are the coordinate vectors of the relevant differentials in the basis \(du_1,ldots,du_N\). Since the covariance functions generate \(K_G\), the preceding identity gives
\[
\operatorname{rank}_L J_0=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G,
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}_L J_1
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G(\lambda_e).
\]
Because \(J_1\) is obtained by adding one row, its rank is either the rank of \(J_0\) or one larger. Moreover,
\[
\operatorname{rank}_LJ_1=\operatorname{rank}_LJ_0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{trdeg}_{K_G}K_G(\lambda_e)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\lambda_e\text{ is algebraic over }K_G.
\]
Thus a rank increase by one is equivalent to transcendence of the queried coordinate.

We next justify the randomized rank computation and its error bound. Acyclicity implies
\[
|D|\leq\frac{n(n-1)}2,
\]
and there are at most \(n(n-1)/2\) bidirected pairs. Hence \(N\leq n^2\). If a Jacobian has generic rank \(q_0>0\), fix one nonzero \(q_0\)-minor. Its total degree is at most
\[
q_0(2n-2)\leq n^2(2n-2)\leq2n^3.
\]
At every specialization the evaluated rank is at most the generic rank; it is equal to the generic rank whenever this fixed minor does not vanish. For a desired rank-error budget \(\eta\in(0,1)\), evaluate \(J_0\) and \(J_1\) at independent source points whose coordinates are uniform in a finite rational set \(S\) with
\[
|S|\geq \frac{4n^3}{\eta}.
\]
The Schwartz--Zippel bound gives probability at most \(\eta/2\) for the vanishing of each fixed maximal minor and hence, by the union bound, probability at most \(\eta\) that either one vanishes. A generic rank-zero matrix is identically zero and introduces no additional failure event. Exact Gaussian elimination at the two specializations therefore returns both generic ranks with probability at least \(1-\eta\). The sampled coordinates, pivot positions, evaluated pivot minors, and identity-test transcript constitute \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\) on the equality branch.

If \(r=0\), the zero-excess clause of the dispatcher invokes the published tree algorithm. By \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}algorithm\mbox{-}transfer}\), it returns the exact \(1\), \(2\), or infinity classification and, in the finite cases, the corresponding one or two fractional affine square-root terms. Allocate error probability \(\delta/2\) to that call and take \(\eta=\delta/2\) for the rank transcript. On the joint success event the exact tree classification and the rank tag agree. Since \(D=T\) has \(|D|=n-1\), a finite tree coordinate also satisfies
\[
d_e(G)\in\{1,2\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
2^{|D|-n+2}=2.
\]
The returned tree expressions are a separate zero-excess payload; the algebraic tag itself remains the rank transcript and degree ceiling stated in the theorem.

If \(r>0\), the dispatcher performs only the Jacobian procedure, with \(\eta=\delta\). On its success event, equality of ranks gives \(d_e(G)<\infty\) by the rank criterion. The established orientation upper bound then gives
\[
d_e(G)\leq2^{|D|-n+2}.
\]
Membership in \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) gives \(|D\setminus T|\leq k\), while a spanning arborescence has \(|T|=n-1\). Because \(T\subseteq D\),
\[
|D|-n+2=|D\setminus T|+1\leq k+1,
\]
and hence
\[
d_e(G)\leq2^{|D|-n+2}\leq2^{k+1}.
\]

If instead the augmented rank is larger, then \(\lambda_e\) is transcendental over \(K_G\). Therefore the \(K_G\)-algebra homomorphism
\[
K_G[t]\longrightarrow A_K,
\qquad t\longmapsto\lambda_e,
\]
is injective. By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), \(A_K\) is an integral domain with fraction field \(L\). The induced morphism
\[
\operatorname{Spec}(A_K)\longrightarrow\mathbb A^1_{K_G}
\]
is consequently dominant, and
\[
\dim\operatorname{Spec}(A_K)
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{K_G}L\geq1
\]
because \(L\) contains the element \(\lambda_e\) transcendental over \(K_G\). The two rank transcripts and a nonzero augmented pivot minor are precisely the source-parametric dominance data recorded in \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\). Thus the infinity tag is correct on the same success event, including when other coordinates leave the full generic fiber positive dimensional.

Finally, constructing the nilpotent inverse circuits, differentiating them, evaluating them, and performing exact Gaussian elimination all require a fixed polynomial number of arithmetic operations and transcript entries in \(n\). Sampling from \(S\) uses \(O(\log n+\log(1/\delta))\) bits per source coordinate. The zero-excess tree call also has polynomial construction time and output length by the cited tree theorem. Since \(n\geq2\) and \(k\geq0\), these bounds are at most
\[
n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))
\]
for a universal constant \(C>0\). The union bound gives total symbolic error at most \(\delta\) in both dispatch branches. No multiplication algebra or eliminant is constructed on the positive-excess algebraic branch, so that branch does not compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\). This proves every asserted tag, bound, dominance, complexity, and output-scope claim.

added_lemmas.statement: For every acyclic tree-shaped mixed graph \(G=(V,D,B)\), meaning that \((V,D)\) is a rooted directed tree while \(B\) is arbitrary, the Gupta--Bl\"aser algorithm decides in randomized polynomial time, for every \(e\in D\), whether \(\lambda_e\) has one, two, or infinitely many generic values. In the first two cases it returns, respectively, one or two fractional affine square-root terms of polynomials representing those values. Its polynomial-identity-testing error can be made at most any prescribed \(\delta\in(0,1)\).

added_lemmas.statement: If \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) and \(|D\setminus T|=0\), then \(D=T\), and the mixed graph is exactly a member of the tree-shaped class treated by Gupta and Bl\"aser, up to their indexing of \(n\) vertices as \(0,\ldots,n-1\) and the transpose convention for \(\Lambda\). For the queried coordinate, their output transfers to the function-field alternatives \(d_e(G)=1\), \(d_e(G)=2\), or \(d_e(G)=\infty\); in the two finite cases its one or two fractional affine square-root terms represent exactly the roots of the queried-coordinate minimal polynomial over an algebraic closure of \(K_G\). This includes every member of \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\), and every tree-shaped mixed graph on \(n\) vertices occurs in \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) and suppose \(|D\setminus T|=0\). Since \(T\subseteq D\), this equality gives \(D=T\). By \(\mathrm{ass:arborescence}\), \((V,T)\), and hence \((V,D)\), is a rooted spanning arborescence. The definition of \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) imposes no restriction on \(B\). Thus \(G\) is a tree-shaped mixed graph in precisely the sense of the cited Gupta--Bl\"aser result. Conversely, if \((V,D)\) is any rooted directed tree, taking \(T=D\) gives \(|D\setminus T|=0\); therefore every such mixed graph, with arbitrary \(B\), belongs to \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\). The source labels its vertices \(0,\ldots,n-1\) after replacing its size parameter by \(n-1\), and its matrix convention is the transpose of the convention used here. Neither relabeling changes an edge coefficient or the solution set of the missing-bidirected residual equations.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:gupta\mbox{-}blaser\mbox{-}tree\mbox{-}algorithm}\) to the fixed edge \(e\). It returns exactly one generic value, exactly two generic values, or infinitely many generic values of \(\lambda_e\), and in either finite case returns the corresponding fractional affine square-root terms.

It remains to translate that generic solution count into the field degree used here. By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), if \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic over \(K_G\), the affine queried-coordinate image of the integral generic fiber over \(\overline{K_G}\) is exactly the root set of the minimal polynomial of \(\lambda_e\). Since \(K_G\) has characteristic zero, that irreducible minimal polynomial is separable. Consequently its number of distinct roots is its degree
\[
[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]=d_e(G).
\]
The one-value and two-value outputs therefore give \(d_e(G)=1\) and \(d_e(G)=2\), respectively, and their displayed terms represent exactly those roots. In the remaining case the generic queried-coordinate image is infinite. Were \(\lambda_e\) algebraic, the same incidence-localization theorem would make that image the finite root set of its minimal polynomial, a contradiction. Hence \(\lambda_e\) is transcendental over \(K_G\) and \(d_e(G)=\infty\). This proves the exact class and output transfer.

proposed.statement:
For every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\), there is a universal \(C>0\) such that \(\mathsf A(G,T,e,\delta)\) returns, with total symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\), exactly one of the following tags. If \(d_e(G)<\infty\), it returns
\[
(\operatorname{algebraic},\mathcal J_{G,e},2^{|D|-n+2}),
\]
where \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\) is a Jacobian-rank transcript certifying algebraicity and
\[
d_e(G)\leq 2^{|D|-n+2}\leq 2^{k+1}.
\]
If \(d_e(G)=\infty\), it returns exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\), where \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) certifies that the queried-coordinate projection of the integral generic fiber is dominant onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\). In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), its construction time and certificate length are at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\). The algebraic tag does not claim to compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\).
